author: Blog Staff
description:
How can you ensure a derived C++ class implements a required method without relying on comments or runtime assertions? This article explores a simpler approach—leaving the method unimplemented in the base class—and demonstrates how C++/WRL, C++/WinRT, and plain C++ catch missing implementations at compile time.

On forcing all derived classes to implement a specific non-virtual method, part 1

by Raymond Chen

From the article:

You may have a base class that implements only partial functionality and relies on the derived class to do the rest. How do you make sure that the derived class does the rest?
